Capped 415°F / 215°C Gas mark 7 · 10% less time 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 10% less time Capped: the converted temperature is above what the unit can reach (400°F basket, 450°F oven-style), so it is held at the maximum and part of the time cut is given back. What recipes use 220°C 220°C (428°F, gas mark 7) is where recipes go for crunch: crispy wings, roast potatoes with a shattering edge, salmon with a firm top, pizza, flatbreads, blistered vegetables. Frozen chips often say it too, but those follow different rules — use frozen mode for them. In the oven it takes this much heat to drive moisture off the surface quickly. An air fryer gets there sooner, so a general recipe converts to 205°C — exactly the 400°F top of a typical basket unit. Everything with the normal cut lands on the ceiling; steak, fish, baked goods and casseroles take a smaller cut, so their converted temperature is above what the basket can reach. The table marks those rows. The failure mode at 220°C: the ceiling Most converters subtract and print the result, even when it is a temperature your air fryer cannot reach. At 220°C that happens for the foods with a gentler cut: the calculation asks for more than 400°F, the basket gives you 400°F, and the food comes out underdone because the time was cut as if the heat were there. This converter clamps the temperature to the ceiling and adds part of the time back, so the capped rows save less time than the rest. The other risk at this heat is smoke. Fat from wings and salmon skin drips onto a very hot drawer, so use an oil with a high smoke point, add marinades with sugar or honey only for the last few minutes, and empty the drawer between batches. Worked example (conventional) A recipe roasts salmon at 220°C for 15 minutes. Fish takes a smaller cut, so its converted temperature is over the basket limit and is held at 205°C (400°F), with the time trimmed only to 12 minutes. Check at 8 minutes: salmon is done at 145°F (63°C) in the thickest part, or when it flakes. An oven-style air fryer has a higher ceiling, so it runs the full 210°C (410°F) for 12 minutes. Worked example (fan) If the recipe gives 200°C fan, the same salmon converts to 195°C (380°F) in a basket air fryer for 14 minutes, checked at 10 minutes. An oven-style unit runs 195°C (385°F) for 14 minutes. The fan input is lower, so more rows may avoid the ceiling. Why oven-style units differ at 220°C An oven-style air fryer usually reaches 450°F, so at 220°C nothing is capped: a general recipe is 210°C (410°F) with about 15% less time, and the gentler-cut foods simply run hotter. The capped rows only appear in the basket column, so check which kind you have before you trust any chart. The converter uses 400°F for basket units and 450°F for oven-style ones. If the dial on yours stops lower, cook at its maximum and allow a little extra time. In °C the recipe is 220°C, and the basket setting is 205°C. For frozen packs, use the frozen mode. Nearby temperatures 200°C oven to air fryer → 425°F oven to air fryer → Oven to air fryer converter (any temperature) → Printable conversion chart → Frozen food mode (packaging instructions) → Convection oven to air fryer → Frequently asked questions What is 220°C in an air fryer? 205°C (400°F) in a basket air fryer for most foods — the basket maximum — with about 12% less time. In an oven-style unit, 210°C (410°F) with about 15% less time. Steak, fish, cakes and casseroles are capped in a basket and keep more of their time. My recipe says 200°C fan — is that the same as 220°C conventional? Yes, fan = conventional − 20°C. The fan input is lower, so more foods avoid the ceiling. What gas mark is 220°C? gas mark 7. The UK dial marks 220°C as gas mark 7. Can I use this for a frozen food pack that says 220°C? No — frozen packs follow different rules (keep the temperature, cut 30% time). Use the frozen mode instead. Why does my air fryer smoke at high temperatures? Fat and sugary marinade drip onto the hot drawer and burn. Use a high-smoke-point oil, add sticky glazes near the end, and empty or wipe the drawer between batches.
